items.staleness: change-coupling — an item whose evidence or requirement record pointer no longer resolves

exit.detail: to ITEMS-DONE.md on DONE or DROPPED

items.growth: unbounded-with-reason — ready-cap 10 bounds the SCHEDULED head and the retirement ratio governs growth; a hard cap on the carrier would force silent drops, which is the failure the carrier exists to prevent

done bodies.staleness: none, declared why: a closure record is history — it accumulates, it does not go stale; growth is the exit question, not a staleness one

exit.recording-act: a ledger decision line naming the compacted range
exit.detail: the retire lane folds bodies past the archive horizon into a summary line — WAVE 4, declared now so the kind has no undeclared stage, not implemented

done bodies.growth: unbounded-with-reason — this is the archive — the BACKLOG-DONE.md split of 2026-08-19 exists because 47% of the live carrier was archive; compaction is its control, not a bound

ledger lines.staleness: none, declared why: the ledger is append-only decision history

exit.recording-act: compaction only — a line whose item is DONE and older than the horizon folds into that body's compaction line

ledger lines.growth: unbounded-with-reason — one line per decision event, no bodies

JOURNAL entries.staleness: change-coupling — a journal entry nothing cites is stale, and a law carrying no journal pointer has no basis; both are read against the citing artifact, never against the entry's age

exit.recording-act: the citing law or workflow's pointer is the record; an entry leaves only through the retire lane's compaction, which names the folded range in a ledger decision line

JOURNAL entries.growth: unbounded-with-reason — one entry per incident, so growth is bounded by the incident rate rather than by a cap — and a cap here would drop the lesson that justifies a law still in force

audits.staleness: change-coupling — an audit whose measured artifact has changed past the citation it carries no longer measures anything current

exit.recording-act: none is taken: an audit is append-only historical (design §4 row 1), and the recording act for a superseded measurement is the newer audit citing the one it overtakes

audits.growth: unbounded-with-reason — append-only historical, one file per measurement; §4 row 1 declares the exit never, so the control on growth is that a measurement is only taken when a question needs it

leak-scan.reason:
OFF, and for the first time that is a real switch rather than a decorative one. The mechanism is now IN this tree — the foreign-path class widened to source scope, the allowlist it needs, and the exemptRoots worktree fix all landed with this line. Before that change the scanner never opened this file at all, so neither this repo's OFF nor the plugin repo's ON described enforcement; the corpus-only behaviour was hardcoded in the copy they share.

WHY NOT ON NOW, measured rather than feared. Run from the lane's tree with the key armed, over the tracked set: 64 findings across 25 files, exit 2. The bootstrap-pair allowlist covers only the scanner and its own suite, which fail the class because they document and fixture the very shapes it matches. Arming the key today would therefore put a guard on the push boundary that fires on 25 files of legitimate work — law 11, and the override reflex trained exactly where it costs most, on a public fork every session pushes to.

THE NAMED EXIT: this flips to ON in THE SAME CHANGE that dispositions all 25 files. Disposition means a verdict per token, and a KEEP is only realized as an allowlist entry — naming it in prose disposes of nothing. The population, from docs/audits/foreign-path-classification-2026-08-26.tsv: 46 distinct tokens, this_repo=9, another_project=7, machine_tool_state=4, synthetic_placeholder=26. Only the another_project bucket is a scrub and that verdict is the operator's; three of those seven landed in cc5565f, three travel with the carrier migration (they sit in files this wave holds byte-identical until `migrate --apply`), and one is a keep the mechanical rule mis-bucketed — a synthetic two-character example in prose about tilde-versus-$HOME spelling. The bucket label is an input to the verdict, never the verdict.

WHY THE FLIP IS NOT ITS OWN LATER COMMIT, and why it is not in the widening commit either. Both orderings leave the declaration and the enforced behaviour disagreeing about what is guarded, in opposite directions: arming before the dispositions blocks legitimate work, and arming afterwards in a separate tidy-up leaves a window in which the tree is clean and the guard says nothing is checked. The widening lane flipped this key in its own worktree, which was correct THERE — that is how the tree carrying the change blocks its own pushes and proves the class fires — and is what this integration restores to the ordering this file already specified for the main checkout.

READING THIS KEY OFF A CLEAN RUN IS AN ERROR. With the class declared false the scanner prints `clean` whatever the files contain, and emits no `degraded:` line, because a declared false is not a could-not-verify. A clean absence-scan result means nothing unless the declaration it read is known. That asymmetry is itself booked as an instrument defect: a declared-off class should print itself NOT EXERCISED.
